brief: A bundle of freshly sharpened pencils standing upright, drawn from a low worm's-eye angle so that the tips stack into stepped setbacks like an Art Deco tower against a pale jade sky. The hexagonal shafts are in lacquered black, cream and racing green, each ferrule a band of brass. Coloured pencil gives the lacquer and the shaved cedar their texture, crisp graphite cores catch the light, and fine gold ink lines trace the verticals. The composition is strictly symmetrical and soaring. The mood is optimistic, streamlined and elegant, with every facet ruled sharp.

A dyer's hands wringing a length of freshly lifted adire cloth, with indigo streaming between the fingers. The fingernails are stained blue-black, and the skin is deep brown with indigo creases. The cloth shows reserved starch-resist patterns, pale and crisp against saturated blue. It is rendered in layered watercolour from Prussian blue to near-black indigo, with whites kept as untouched paper, as if resisted. Drips, beads of dye and a bronze oxidation sheen are rendered precisely. The background is a dark clay vat rim. The light is earthy and close, the mood tactile and laborious.

A half-spent toothpaste tube, wrung and creased from the bottom, a ribbon of striped paste curling from its open mouth. It is built like a hand-pulled screenprint from flat, opaque layers of process cyan, warm vermilion, mint and a mid-grey. Each separation is slightly misregistered, so thin slivers of paper and overprint show at the edges. Despite the flatness, the crumpled foil reads as utterly real through the logic of the separations: highlight, midtone and crease shadow. The tube floats on a solid butter-yellow field. The surface is matte and graphic, the edges crisp.

Hundreds of tiny clear and mother-of-pearl shirt buttons, arranged with a microscopist's obsessive patience into concentric rosettes and spoked wheels on an inky blue-black ground, like a Victorian diatom slide. Darkfield lighting: each button is drawn only by its lit rim, thread holes and bevelled lip, picked out in fine white and pale silver pen over the black. Faint ghosts of iridescence in lilac and celadon sit inside the domes. The symmetry is almost perfect, but one button is tipped on its edge. The surface is clinical and airless, every edge razor-sharp, the whole piece intimate as a specimen under glass.

A boxer in a dim gym taping his hands, framed tight on the fists and forearms, the background a grimy blur of ropes. The colour is drained to a gunmetal silver-green, with skin almost colourless and blacks crushed hard. It is made of charcoal and cool grey washes, with metallic silver pencil on the highlights of sweat and veins. The white wraps are the brightest thing, frayed and stained. The contrast is harsh and grainy, as if the film were pushed. The mood is grim, focused and exhausted, with gritty edges and nothing pretty.

An overhead view of an old haberdasher's drawer divided into a strict grid of square wooden compartments. Each cell holds one spool of thread, some with a snipped tail, some half-unwound into a tiny nest. The palette echoes Andean weaving: cochineal crimson, ochre, black, cream and mustard. Dense, directional coloured-pencil hatching renders every wrapped filament and the wood grain between cells. The grid repeats with variations, like tocapu squares, and no two units are alike. The light is flat and even, the mood archival and orderly, the texture almost touchable.

An extreme close-up of a grilled hot dog in a split bun with a glossy zigzag of mustard, cropped off the edges. The whole image is built from graduated Ben-Day dots in process magenta, yellow, cyan and black. The dots are dense and overlapping in the char marks, sparse in the bun's highlights. Seen up close, it is pure stippled pen dots. From a distance, it resolves into greasy, photographic realism: blistered skin, sesame-free crumb, a drip about to fall. There are no outlines, only dot density. It is brash, appetising and slightly absurd.

Total darkness, broken by a single hard oval of follow-spot light on the ice. Inside it are a figure skater's boot and blade, caught mid-stop, carving a crescent and throwing a fan of shaved ice. The darkness is dense charcoal mass. The lit zone is white and cool steel blue, with sprayed specks of ice crystal frozen in the air. Laces, scuffed white leather and blade-scratches are rendered with forensic sharpness at the spotlight's edge, then cut off abruptly. The mood is suspense and applause just before it happens, theatrical and stark.

Seen from directly above: a worn white cotton skipping rope, dropped by a child, has fallen into looping, kolam-like curves around an even grid of smooth river pebbles on freshly swept red-earth ground. It is drawn in dry soft pencil and white chalk pastel over a burnt-sienna, terracotta-toned ground. The broom striations in the dust run in parallel arcs. The rope's twisted fibres, frayed tips and wooden handles are rendered with meticulous texture. Morning light rakes low from one side, so each pebble throws a short umber shadow. The image is calm, rhythmic and sun-warmed, with dusty edges.

A long steel lei needle mid-threading. Popcorn puffs and glossy cranberries alternate along a cotton thread that snakes diagonally across a warm koa-wood table. Hands are only implied at the frame's edge. It is drawn in soft pencil with transparent watercolour: buttery cream kernels with ragged hull shards, cranberries in deep alizarin with a pinpoint shine, and the thread slightly fuzzy. Loose popcorn and stray hulls sit in a shallow bowl, out of the pattern. The rhythm is a repeated unit, counted and patient. The light comes from a side window, gentle and homely, made with care.

A dented, stacked steel tiffin carrier, every tier hand-painted the way rickshaw panels are: candy-apple red, parrot green and saffron, with peacocks and roses. It is rendered with glossy enamel-like marker fills and hard specular streaks. The perspective is slightly frontal and theatrical. Behind it, a scalloped border of tin-cut flowers, mirror dots and stripes in turquoise and hot pink frames the scene like a painted backboard. Scuffs reveal bare metal, and a crusted dal stain sits on the latch. The palette is loud and lacquered, the edges crisp, the realism festive and proud.

A carver's workbench seen from above, scattered with long, curling wood shavings. Their spirals naturally repeat in koru-like rhythms across the plank, echoing painted rafter patterns. The palette is red ochre, bone white and charcoal black: the totara shavings have ochre-pink edges, the bench is dark, and the chisel lies white-handled at one side. Ink line and flat marker build the rhythm, with fine hatching for the grain and translucent edges where the shavings thin out. The composition is a flowing horizontal band, balanced and repeating, but every curl is individually and believably real.

A sawmill interior where one hard shaft of morning light slants through a gap in the plank wall and cuts diagonally across a frame of airborne sawdust. In its path sits a toothed circular blade, each tooth's bevel and rust bloom sharp. The medium is soft compressed charcoal pushed into dense burnt-umber darkness. The beam is lifted out as a warm bone-white wedge, filled with a fine spray of suspended motes. Outside the beam everything melts into velvety shadow. Inside it, raw sienna wood fibres, pine curls and a fingerprint smudge on the steel read with forensic clarity.

A rose-ringed parrot gripping a split guava. Every form is enclosed in the double outline typical of Madhubani, and the gap between the lines is filled with tiny dashes. Inside those borders, fine pen hatching builds feathers in hyperreal detail, each barb visible in parrot green and turmeric. The guava flesh is a glistening coral-pink, with seeds rendered individually. The background is a dense lattice of leaves in lamp-black and vermilion line, with no empty space anywhere. The folk structure stays strict, while the rendering inside each cell is photographic.

A patisserie window constructed like a receding opera set of painted flats and gauze scrims. In the foreground sits a hyperreal tiered cake with piped rosettes and glossy ganache. Behind it, cut-edge planes of shelves, jars and lettered awnings step back in layers. Each plane is lit by imagined limelight from below, so the undersides glow pale gold and the tops fall into rose-violet shadow. Scenic watercolour washes and scumbled dry-brush give the backdrops a theatrical softness. The cake, by contrast, is rendered in razor-precise detail. Thin veils of translucent wash between layers suggest hanging gauze.

A steam iron resting on its heel on a crumpled linen sheet, with steam unfurling upward. It is rendered like an early photogravure: warm sepia-black ink over cream paper, with a fine aquatint grain throughout. Charcoal-like massing builds the deep velvety blacks of the soleplate and cord. Delicate spray stipple carries the steam's soft gradations so that it dissolves into the paper. Every linen crease is softly modelled, with plate-tone haze at the edges and slightly heavier inking at the corners. The focus is shallow and pictorialist, and the hyperreal detail lives only in the chrome's dull reflection.

A single tiger prawn curled into the teardrop swell and hooked tip of a paisley boteh. It rests on crushed ice against a deep indigo cloth. Coloured pencil builds the shell to obsessive realism: translucent grey-blue segments, coral-pink joints and fine feathered legs. The antennae sweep out as long hairline curves that echo paisley tendrils. The ice is layered with tiny burnished whites and meltwater sheen. Within the shell, minute repeated chevrons and dots of pigment read as both natural texture and ornamental fill. The composition is offset low-left, and the antennae arc across empty cloth.

The scene is seen through a window whose thick black muntins form an asymmetric grid. Behind it, a washing line holds plastic clothes pegs in pure red, yellow and blue, clipped to white cotton. Each pane crops the scene differently. Some are filled almost entirely by one hyperreal peg, rendered in coloured pencil with moulded seams, a rusted spring and a pinched fabric fold. Others show only bare white sky. Flat gouache-like watercolour paints the black bars with crisp edges. The composition balances Mondrian proportions against tactile, everyday detail.

A hyperreal open palm of a sun-weathered hand, seen from above, stands in for a treasure map. Its deep lines and creases read as rivers and coastlines, and calluses rise like islands. A dotted biro trail winds from the wrist toward a small inked X near the base of the fingers. Sepia pen hatching carries every pore and skin ridge. Tea-coloured watercolour washes stain it like old parchment. A tiny compass rose is drawn on the thumb.

A city pedestrian footbridge over a canal, with two pigeons wheeling above it. It is rendered entirely in cobalt monochrome on cream, echoing the willow-pattern composition, but drawn with documentary precision. The surface is built from dense pen stipple and fine engraved line, mimicking transfer-printed dots. A soft cobalt watercolour bleed gathers at the edges, like glaze blur. The railing bolts, graffiti tags, ripples and pigeon feathers are all hyperreal, yet the tonal logic is a single blue. A decorative scalloped border band frames the scene loosely.
